quote: Was bedeutet es wenn die Invariante verschwindet, welche auftritt, wenn wir diese Covariante zweimal bilden.
english: What does it mean if the invariant vanishes which arises when we form this covariant twice?
topic: A list of research ideas in invariant theory: groups of operations arising from irrational covariants, covariants defined by vanishing transvectants of binary forms of degree 7 and 10, a generalisation of Gordan's problem on sextic forms, vanishing transvectants of a form with its transform, re-proving a theorem of the dissertation by infinitesimal transformations, and a Lagrange problem on solving a binary form equal to a power of 2 in integers.

triage.modern_statement: Here is the most plausible modern reading. Let f be a binary form and C(f) a covariant built from f, for example a transvectant (f,f)_k. Apply the same construction to C(f), so you get C(C(f)), and suppose the result is an invariant I(f). The note asks what geometric or algebraic condition on f is expressed by I(f) = 0. The trouble is that 'this covariant' (diese Covariante) refers back to an earlier item on the page, maybe one of the covariants from vanishing transvectants of degree-7 or degree-10 forms, or an irrational covariant. Without the page I can't tell which construction is meant. That leaves the degree of f, the covariant and the invariant all undetermined.
triage.answered_by: Can't be determined, because the question can't be pinned down without the preceding entry on the page. None of my searches tied this note to Hilbert's 23 problems, the 24th problem, or any later named result.

evidence.claim: Cod. Ms. D. Hilbert 600 is Hilbert's scientific diary (wissenschaftliches Tagebuch) in the Göttingen Nachlass. This confirms the source but says nothing about the content of this note.
The Kalliope finding aid dates the diary to about 1886–1912 and describes it as notes on general and specific problems in mathematics.
General background: covariants of binary forms are generated by iterated transvectants (Gordan's theorem). This is the setting in which 'forming a covariant twice' would yield an invariant.

General background: there is modern work on loci of forms defined by the vanishing of transvectants, such as Brill–Gordan loci. This is the kind of question the note gestures at, but no source links it to this note.

triage.why: The note points back to an unnamed covariant ('this covariant') from a nearby item, so the actual question can't be reconstructed from the text alone. I found no sources discussing this diary entry, and nothing connects it to a published Hilbert problem or a later result. Questions about what it means for an iterated covariant or invariant to vanish (that is, describing such loci) belong to classical invariant theory, and work on transvectant-defined loci continues. But I can't say that this specific question was answered or is still open.
